benchmark.name: Lending Desk Bench
benchmark.tagline: Can a flash-class coding agent finish a real App Router feature under a strict contract?
benchmark.purpose: Hermetic evaluation of multi-file Next.js / React product work matching Reading Advantage monorepo practice — not trivia or greenfield toys.
audiences: Engineering leads choosing models for agentic coding
Eval / platform teams measuring cost vs quality
Staff engineers who care about auth, races, and App Router pitfalls

arms.a: Fixture + prompt only (no skills). Primary fair comparison.
arms.b: Same task with AGENTS.md + five skills. Experimental; not averaged into Arm A rankings when incomplete.

scoring.note: Soft tiers scale higher-tier credit by lower-tier rates (no binary cliff at 90% Tier 0). Advisory checks never affect totals.

A.title: Business rules
A.why: Pure domain logic with a fixed clock. Wrong here means every status badge and filter lies.

B.title: UI composition
B.why: Reusable card: link, alt text, loan badge. List consistency and accessibility.

C.title: Catalogue & data fetching
C.why: List page with search/category filters and parallel reads — everyday App Router list work.

D.title: Detail & history
D.why: Dynamic route, not-found, metadata, ordered loan history with live status.

E.title: Interactive forms
E.why: Checkout/return UX: pending labels, optimistic UI, error display.

F.title: Mutations & auth
F.why: Server Actions must authorize, validate, and persist correctly.

G.title: HTTP API contract
G.why: REST handler filters, status codes, conflicts, freshness.

H.title: Resilience UX
H.why: loading.tsx and error.tsx — streaming shells and failure boundaries.

M.title: Process closeout
M.why: Did the agent finish the phased plan and metadata?

P.title: Adversarial probes
P.why: Hidden checks: revalidation, races, waterfalls, N+1, credential leak.

ADV.title: Advisory (unscored)
ADV.why: React 19 form idioms (useActionState / useOptimistic). Never in the numeric total.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash
models.summary: Best flash result on this task — near-reference functional quality at very low cost.

models.name: Ling 3.0 Flash
models.summary: Competitive mid-pack score; relatively stronger on forms/auth than peers, weaker on probes.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.summary: Highest API spend and output volume; strong catalogue/API surface, weaker mutation/form path.

models.name: Qwen 3.7 Flash
models.summary: Solid mid-pack; large input/cache footprint. Arm B experiment is separate and not averaged in.

models.name: MiMo V2.5
models.summary: Cheapest run; more regressions on probes and interactive UI.

arm_b.name: Qwen 3.7 Flash (Arm B experiment)
arm_b.summary: Only Arm B run in this corpus (skills mounted). Not ranked against Arm A models.
